Extended the deadline for eligible owner-occupiers to sell their previous home from 12 to 18 months under mortgage-rule exemptions.
Reported targeted tax audits of property transactions, closed loopholes, and investigated real-estate-related tax avoidance.
Outlined housing-tax reform ideas still under consideration rather than announcing a new tax rate.
Revised the filing guidelines for Land-Housing Integrated Income Tax 2.0
Approved the Housing Tax Differential Rate 2.0 plan with higher rates for multiple non-owner-occupied homes.
Proposed lower property-tax rates for qualifying single owner-occupied homes and certain rented or inherited properties.
Enhanced programs for first-home loans with higher loan limits, longer repayment and grace periods, and additional interest subsidies.
Published draft legislative amendments specifying the previously announced House Tax 2.0 reform and its administration.
Announced executive approval of a draft House Tax 2.0 bill, pending final legislative enactment.
Announced legislative passage of higher progressive house-tax rates on multiple non-owner-occupied and vacant homes.
Announced legislative passage of preferential house-tax rates for qualifying single owner-occupied and eligible rented properties.
Explained the existing youth mortgage subsidy and discussed strengthening post-loan checks against misuse without a finalized new rule.
Clarified existing House Tax 2.0 household-registration requirements without announcing a new tax-rate change.
Approved draft anti-speculation proposals restricting presale-contract transfers and corporate home purchases and penalizing market manipulation.

Announced the July 2023 start of anti-speculation measures under the amended Equalization of Land Rights Act.
Announced the July 2023 start of expanded rental subsidies for qualifying households.
Announced the July 2023 rollout of Social Housing Subleasing and Management 4.0.
Announced inspections against misleading housing marketing and enforcement of existing anti-speculation penalties.
Reported rental-subsidy outcomes and a proposed program extension, without confirming a newly approved subsidy change.
Reaffirmed existing statutory real-estate lending limits and required sound bank oversight without changing the legal ceiling.
Excluded newly disbursed eligible youth home loans from statutory bank real-estate lending caps.
Announced passage of House-and-Land Tax 2.0, increasing tax rates on short-term property resales and closing avoidance routes.
Approved implementing rules for corporate housing-purchase permits, presale-contract transfer exemptions, and anti-speculation reporting rewards.
Restricted eligible applicants to one subsidized youth home loan from the stated cutoff date.
Strengthened public-bank loan screening, owner-occupancy declarations, and post-loan enforcement for subsidized youth mortgages.
Announced new rental electricity billing rules capping landlord charges and requiring disclosure of utility costs.
